test_plan.strategy: The verdict is a pure function, so its rules are unit-tested directly with crafted probe snapshots — including the two cases the design argues hardest about: a single dropped ping must NOT flap the tile (ADR-2) and a VPN tunnel must NOT double-count throughput (ADR-3). The tile's markup is tested by rendering the real partial through renderPartial (the same path SSE uses), asserting the collapsed disclosure, the absorbed WAN chip and the surviving BG-072 filter. Two regression cases guard the neighbouring tiles and the nil-safety of the SSE render path, because a panic here would kill the dashboard for every connected client.
test_plan.coverage_goal: Every acceptance criterion of FR-085/086/087 and the three NFRs has a traced, passing test; zero regressions in the 86 existing test cases.

test_cases.title: All probes healthy → Stable
test_cases.given: probes gateway(ok,0% loss,1.4ms), 1.1.1.1(ok,0%,12ms), 8.8.8.8(ok,0%,14ms), dns(ok,0%,11ms) and WAN state=up
test_cases.then: Verdict == 'stable' and the reason mentions 'WAN up' and 0% loss
test_cases.expected_result: LinkState{Verdict:'stable'} with a reason naming WAN up and 0% loss

test_cases.title: A probe at 15% loss → Unstable, and the reason names the failing target
test_cases.given: gateway ok at 0% loss, but 8.8.8.8 reports 15% loss (3 of its 20-sample window)
test_cases.then: Verdict == 'unstable', WorstLoss == 15, and Reason contains '8.8.8.8' and '15%'

test_cases.title: WAN monitor down → Offline
test_cases.given: every probe still answers, but the WAN monitor reports state 'down'
test_cases.then: Verdict == 'offline' — the WAN monitor is the authority and it needs 3 consecutive failures to flip, so this is not a flap

test_cases.title: Gateway unreachable → Offline, not merely Unstable
test_cases.given: the gateway probe reports status 'timeout' while off-box targets still answer
test_cases.then: Verdict == 'offline' — a box that cannot reach its own gateway has a broken LAN, a different problem from a lossy internet path
test_cases.expected_result: LinkState{Verdict:'offline'} driven by the gateway, not by the off-box targets

test_cases.title: No probes configured → no verdict claimed
test_cases.given: an empty probe list (and a nil WAN snapshot)
test_cases.then: Verdict == 'unknown' — the tile must not claim a state it cannot know, and must not panic on the nil inputs

test_cases.title: A single dropped ping (5% loss) does NOT flip the tile to Unstable
test_cases.given: every probe ok, but one reports 5% loss — exactly one dropped packet in its 20-sample window
test_cases.then: Verdict == 'stable' — a >0% rule would flap on one lost packet and train the admin to ignore the tile (ADR-2)

test_cases.title: WAN state lives in the tile; the standalone chip is gone
test_cases.then: the tile's subtitle contains 'WAN up' and the partial contains no standalone WAN chip element below the metric grid
test_cases.expected_result: subtitle contains WAN up; the old chip markup is absent

test_cases.title: WAN down: the tile reads Offline and there is still no second WAN element
test_cases.then: the tile reads Offline and the page contains no standalone WAN chip — the tile is the single source of WAN truth
test_cases.expected_result: tile shows Offline; no duplicate WAN element anywhere in the partial

test_cases.title: No WAN snapshot: nothing is claimed and the template does not crash
test_cases.given: a nil WAN snapshot (the monitor never observed anything yet)
test_cases.then: the tile renders without claiming a WAN state, and the template executes without error
test_cases.expected_result: partial renders non-empty HTML; no 'WAN up'/'WAN down' text; no template error

test_cases.title: The other four tiles are untouched
test_cases.given: a snapshot with CPU 22.2%, RAM 45.7%, disk and temp populated
test_cases.then: CPU, Memory, Disk and Temp still render their values with their existing thresholds
test_cases.expected_result: all four neighbouring tiles render unchanged alongside the new Network tile

test_cases.title: A nil probe entry never panics the SSE render
test_cases.given: a probe slice containing a nil element
test_cases.then: the nil entry is skipped and a verdict is still returned — a panic here would kill the dashboard for every connected client
test_cases.expected_result: no panic; a valid LinkState is returned

test_cases.title: Full page flow: an authenticated admin loads the dashboard and gets the new tile
test_cases.given: a running server with an admin user (and no probes wired, as in a fresh box)
test_cases.when: the client logs in at POST /login and then GETs /
test_cases.then: status 200; the dashboard HTML contains the Network tile with its collapsed per-interface disclosure, and contains NO standalone WAN chip element
test_cases.expected_result: dashboard renders through the PAGE template path (not the SSE path) with the new tile and without the orphan chip

test_cases.title: Full SSE flow: the live metrics event carries the new tile through the OTHER FuncMap (re-pointed from AC-086-002 when FR-086 was retired; the test asserts the tile renders through the SSE FuncMap, which is FR-085 behaviour)
test_cases.given: an authenticated session and the SSE broadcast path
test_cases.when: buildSharedSSEEvents renders the metrics event the browser swaps into the page
test_cases.then: the event body contains the Network tile's verdict markup and its collapsed disclosure — proving the new template funcs are registered in BOTH FuncMaps (templates.go carries two; registering in one silently breaks the other path)
test_cases.expected_result: the SSE metrics event renders the tile without a template error

test_cases.title: Absorbing the WAN chip introduces no new type scale or colour
preconditions: The dashboard partial renders through the SSE FuncMap
test_cases.given: A healthy Pi with WAN up and the full interface list
test_cases.when: sse-metrics.html renders and the Network tile is isolated
test_cases.then: The WAN phrase sits on the reason line under the shared subtitle tokens (text-xs text-text-muted); the chip's wrapper markup is absent; and outside the value line the tile introduces no other type scale or weight
steps: Render the partial with WAN up
Assert the reason line carries class="text-xs text-text-muted truncate"
Assert the chip's background and label markup are absent
Strip the value classes and assert no other size or weight token appears
test_cases.expected_result: WAN text on the existing subtitle tokens, chip markup gone, no new size/colour introduced

test_cases.title: BG-073 happy path: sparkline history is read back by probe label (traced to AC-085-002 — the degraded-link case the sparklines are the drill-down for; NFR-089b is a Regression NFR with no acceptance-criterion id of its own, so it borrows one, as TC-NT-088h/088f do for NFR-088b)
preconditions: A test server with its database
test_cases.given: Two net samples stored keyed by the probe LABEL 'gateway', the way main.go stores them
test_cases.when: The dashboard reads recent samples for the sparkline
test_cases.then: Reading by label returns both rows and computeRTTSeries yields a two-point series; reading by the resolved IP 192.168.1.1 returns nothing, which is what the old code did
steps: Assert two rows and a two-point series
test_cases.expected_result: History is label-keyed; the sparkline finds its samples

test_cases.title: BG-073 negative: reading probe history by the resolved IP finds nothing
preconditions: A test server with its database
test_cases.given: One net sample stored keyed by the probe LABEL 'gateway'
test_cases.when: History is queried by the resolved IP 192.168.1.1 and then by the label
test_cases.then: The IP query returns nothing — the original bug — while the label query returns the sample
steps: Query RecentNetSamples('gateway') and assert one row
test_cases.expected_result: IP query empty, label query returns 1 row

test_cases.title: BG-073 edge: a label with no history yet renders instead of panicking
preconditions: A test server with its database
test_cases.given: A probe label that has never sampled — a freshly added target, or the first minutes after a restart
test_cases.when: computeRTTSeries runs over the empty row set and the template renders the sparkline
test_cases.then: The series is empty, min/max/avg are zero, and sparklineSVG does not panic
steps: Query history for an unknown label and assert no rows
Call computeRTTSeries and assert an empty series with zero stats
Assert sparklineSVG does not panic on the empty series
test_cases.expected_result: Empty series, zero stats, sparkline renders without panic
